0.content:
Ayato is head of the Kamisato Clan and Yashiro Commissioner, and Thoma's lord. Ten years ago, amid a succession dispute after his parents' deaths, Ayato warned Thoma to leave if he did not want to be drawn into the clan's troubles. He says now that this was partly to see where Thoma stood. Thoma refused and received his Vision that night. Ayato says few people have his complete trust, and Thoma is one of them. Thoma, for his part, keeps an eye on Ayato at home and says his lord takes no joy in political battles; for him they are "a matter of duty".

Ayato's own story notes that he once wondered whether the outlander Thoma would consider other options should the clan truly fall. He also lets Thoma bend the rules to obtain Shuumatsuban intelligence in emergencies. Ayato is a mischievous master. According to Hiratsuka, whenever Ayato spends time with Thoma he ropes him into eating strange food, so Thoma has come to dread seeing him coming. The Traveler once found the two of them in the middle of a chess game (2.6).

1.content:
Thoma is Ayaka's attendant and friend; she calls him a dear friend whose sunny disposition lifts her spirits, another brother and a full member of the clan. He and Yoimiya are her only known friends before the Traveler. He carries out her wishes, and in 2.0 he was her go-between with the Traveler. When he was seized for the Vision Hunt Ceremony she wanted to rescue him herself, remembering how they had all just eaten hotpot together, but the Traveler went instead to protect the Yashiro Commission's neutrality. He wishes she would voice her own opinions more and advises friends to keep asking for them.

In 2025 she asked Thoma to teach her foreign weaving techniques so she could knit a scarf for the Traveler in Nod-Krai (birthday mail).

2.content:
Beidou left the Traveler in Thoma's care at Ritou. He tested their resolve with a deliberately impossible path out of the port, then apologised and took them to Ayaka. After the Traveler fought the Raiden Shogun at the Vision Hunt Ceremony to save his Vision, he swore them his weapon and his loyalty, promising to fight for them "no matter what". He treats them as a close friend: he invites them to birthday parties, worries they are not eating properly on the road, and admits his homesickness to them.

In 5.7 he enjoyed a reunion with the Traveler at Angel's Share and joked that it felt odd to be welcomed home by the Honorary Knight. In 2026 he called them his "farthest friend", now in Nod-Krai.

3.content:
In the 2.0 Archon Quest the Tenryou Commission took Thoma to the Statue of the Omnipresent God to be the 100th Vision bearer stripped under the Vision Hunt Decree, at a ceremony the Raiden Shogun attended in person. His Vision was already floating toward her hand when the Traveler intercepted it. The Shogun overwhelmed the Traveler; Thoma freed himself, hurled a polearm at her and fled carrying the Traveler. Both became wanted. He sent the Traveler to the Watatsumi resistance and hid at Komore Teahouse, inside Yashiro territory. He later said that without the Traveler he would have lost his Vision "and with it all my aspirations".

Itto, hearing of it, was indignant that Thoma got "his own special ceremony". After the decree was repealed (2.1), Thoma came out of hiding; the vacation in his Hangout Event follows his release from the teahouse.

4.content:
Thoma's mother, Ulrike, is a Mondstadt-born Knight of Favonius, described by Kaeya as free-spirited, thoughtful, gentle and kind, "the very model of a Knight", and able to drink most sailors under the table. Her favourite tavern is Angel's Share. After the Sakoku Decree lifted, she and Thoma wrote often; she once demanded Inazuman wines to taste what he drinks. By 5.7 she had received orders to join Grand Master Varka's expedition camp in Nod-Krai, and the Knights threw her a packed farewell party. His father is Inazuman, taught him loyalty and righteousness, and returned to Inazuma; Thoma could never find him there.

Kaeya says the generosity runs in the family: "like mother, like son".

5.content: In the 5.7 anecdotes (Travelers' Tales, permanent), Thoma helped the Yashiro Commission run housekeeping training and licensing exams to improve job prospects, enrolling Kuki Shinobu, who planned to tutor the Arataki Gang. Ayato then approved a long vacation and Thoma went home to Mondstadt for the first time in years. He sorted his mother's documents and mementos, repaired and cleaned the empty house, and at Angel's Share ran into Kaeya. One glass of Kaeya's recommended Death After Noon turned him beet-red. They swapped childhood stories of sneaking "grown-up drinks", talked youkai legends over non-alcoholic cider, and exchanged addresses (Knights of Favonius; Yashiro Commission). He invited Kaeya to his next birthday (January 2026); Kaeya replied that Inazuma is a long way to come and he might not make it in time, and sent a gift with his letter.

6.content: Worried his father could not get Mondstadt wine in Inazuma, a young Thoma sailed alone with a boat full of Dandelion Wine. A huge wave capsized it, and he drifted unconscious until he washed up on an Inazuman beach. He had no money, no family and no connections. He faced it with optimism, but despite his efforts never found his father. At his most difficult moment he met someone worthy of his "loyalty" (unnamed in the story, but by every indication the Kamisato Clan), and owing them his survival gave him his sense of "repayment".

7.comment: Thoma: Ritou and the International Trade Association
7.content: Thoma looked after Ritou's stranded foreign merchants during the Sakoku era. He relates to their homesickness but notes that they never tried to integrate, so Inazumans always saw them as outsiders. He sent the Traveler to help his friend Kurisu, president of the Association, against a Kanjou Commission Crystal Marrow tax scheme. When a Kanjou official tried to arrest the protesting merchants, Thoma stopped it with a Yashiro Commission card and an ornate fan that made the officer back down for fear of offending "her".

8.content: Thoma feeds every stray he meets and says one whistle brings puppies and kittens running. Taroumaru, the dog of Komore Teahouse, is his friend; Thoma imitated him to prank the Traveler. In his Hangout Event he tried to feed a wary Shuumatsuban ninja dog, Inu Shoushou, tasting the food himself to prove it was safe. They learned its owner had gone on a dangerous mission at sea and would not return. In another ending he knits sweaters for strays, and one does not quite fit.

9.content: Thoma explains Inazuma to newcomers as the Nation of Eternity, a god keeping the land in stasis through the Tri-Commission and the Sakoku Decree, and calls it "my own limited understanding". Mondstadters revere Barbatos; Inazumans love, respect and fear their Shogun. He does not resent her for nearly taking his Vision, but neither understands nor agrees with sacrificing people's aspirations for eternity. In 2.1, with Kujou Kamaji at the statue, he worried about the Shogun's seclusion and the encroaching storms.
